text:
Mira.Sec: Quick follow-up on the authn/authz RFC — proposing a lightweight token-exchange pattern for service->service calls with narrow-scoped delegated keys. TL;DR: exchange long-lived API keys for short-lived, audience-bound tokens at the auth broker, with explicit project/org scoping. Thoughts?

 daniel.eng: +1 on moving to short-lived tokens. Can we avoid adding another DB lookup per request?

 alex.ops: Suggestion: mint exchange tokens with embedded scopes and a cheap signature verification (JWT-ish) so runtime can verify locally. Keep a revocation list for immediate invalidation.

 dinesh.infra: revocation list at scale is painful. Maybe use short TTL (1-5m) and accept eventual revocation; critical burst ops can fallback to introspect endpoint.

 daniel.eng: tradeoff: local verify = faster, but we need stable key rotation for the broker and key distribution to all runtimes. How do we push new keys without redeploys?

 Mira.Sec: rotate broker signing keys weekly by default, publish keys to our internal JWKS endpoint; runtimes fetch with cache-control and jitter. For hot rotations, publish v2 key and allow a 1 grace window.

 sasha.pm: From product POV we need clear migration for existing API keys used by customers. What's the opt-in path vs automatic?

 Mira.Sec: plan A: opt-in SDK that exchanges customer API key for ephemeral token transparently. plan B (enterprise): mTLS or HSM-backed service tokens for Private deployments. We'll document both.

 alex.ops: We should define the exact token shape. Proposal: {"iss":"auth-broker","sub":"svc:project:svc-name","aud":"service-x","exp":<unix> ,"scopes":["read:models","embed:create"],"org":"org-123","proj":"proj-456"}. Signed with rotating key id in header.

 daniel.eng: + add "orig_kid" claim if we want to trace back to the issuing API key for billing/audit. Keep token small — avoid big metadata.

 dinesh.infra: rate limiting: exchanged tokens inherit the rate limits of the original key by default. Need a mapping layer so project quotas apply even after exchange.

 Mira.Sec: noted. We'll route exchange requests through quota service which stamps quota-id into token claim. That avoids a second lookup on each request, just verify claim.

 token-bot: :white_check_mark: Token policy draft uploaded: https://redwood.internal/docs/auth/token-exchange-draft (version 0.1)

 sasha.pm: What about service impersonation/act-as patterns? Customers asked for a way to run jobs on behalf of users without exposing user creds.

 daniel.eng: implement act-as via a separate audience and require explicit consent/claim from the original user token. Short-lived, aud=job-runner, scope limited. Audit logs mandatory.

 Mira.Sec: open questions we should track in RFC follow-up: 1) recommended TTL ranges by workload, 2) revocation semantics and emergencies, 3) migration path for public API keys, 4) SDK support and interceptors.

 alex.ops: Also call out cross-project delegation patterns: should tokens carry a "delegation_chain" claim for nested handoffs, or do we require the broker to mint fresh tokens at each hop? My vote: mint fresh tokens at each hop and keep chain in audit logs to avoid unbounded token size.

 dinesh.infra: agree. fresh tokens simplifies scope reduction at each hop. We should also rate-limit exchange endpoints to avoid token amplification attacks.

 Mira.Sec: action items: - daniel.eng to prototype local verify + jwks cache pattern (ETA 2w) - dinesh.infra to propose revocation/emergency flow (ETA 1w) - alex.ops to draft token shape + rotation policy (ETA 4d) - sasha.pm to write migration comms for customers (ETA 1w)

 daniel.eng: I'll drop a tiny PoC repo with verification lib and caching hook.

 sasha.pm: will sync with growth for messaging. keep comms simple: "exchanging keys for short-lived tokens to improve security and reliability"

 Mira.Sec: thanks all. If no objections within 48h we'll fold these items into the RFC and start an implementation PR. :thumbsup:

 alex.ops: quick nit: include example exchange curl in the RFC. e.g.:

 ```
 POST /v1/token/exchange HTTP/1.1
 Authorization: ApiKey abcd...
 Content-Type: application/json

 {"aud":"service-x","scopes":["read:models"],"ttl":300}
```

 Mira.Sec: included. I'll upload the RFC follow-up after the prototype lands.

 dinesh.infra: :eyes: tagging infra on the draft for capacity planning.

 token-bot: draft updated in docs (version 0.2) https://redwood.internal/docs/auth/token-exchange-draft/v0.2

 Mira.Sec: end of thread — thanks everyone."
